query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Preheating the build plate and powder bed to 250 °C during PBF-LB of equimolar CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy-alloy powder will reduce thermal gradients and residual stresses, promoting a uniform, equiaxed grain structure with fewer microcracks and pores, thereby improving dimensional precision and mechanical integrity.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar CoCrFeNiMn powder bed at ambient temperature, standard PBF-LB parameters (200 W laser, 40 µm layer thickness, 800 mm/s scan speed, 67° layer‐to‐layer rotation).
generation.intervention: Maintain build plate and surrounding powder bed at 250 °C throughout the PBF-LB build.
generation.conditions: PBF-LB on a commercial machine (e.g. EOS M290), inert Ar atmosphere, build plate preheated and held at 250 °C, standard scan strategy and powder layer parameters.
generation.structural_mediator: Reduced residual stress and thermal gradient leading to a fine, uniform equiaxed grain microstructure with minimal microcracks and porosity.
generation.mechanism: Elevated base temperature lowers cooling rates and thermal gradients, reducing stress concentrations that nucleate cracks and pores; promotes homogeneous nucleation of equiaxed grains rather than columnar growth.
generation.predicted_outcome: Warpage reduced by ≥30%, bulk porosity reduced by ≥25%, ultimate tensile strength increased by ~5–10%, elongation to failure increased by ~10% relative to baseline builds without preheating.
generation.baseline: Standard PBF-LB builds at ambient build-plate temperature exhibit ~0.8 ± 0.2% porosity, warpage of ~0.5 mm over a 50 mm length, UTS ~650 MPa, elongation ~20%.
generation.boundary: Holds for equimolar CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloys processed by PBF-LB under 200–300 W laser power, 30–50 µm layer thickness, scan speeds of 600–1000 mm/s; may not apply to other HEA compositions or to DED processes.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of improvement is estimated from analogous results in Ni-base superalloys and Ti-6Al-4V; direct HEA data is lacking, so actual gains may vary by ±10 percentage points.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of dog‐bone and rectangular coupons (n≥5 each) of CoCrFeNiMn via PBF-LB: one with build-plate at ambient temp, one with build-plate at 250 °C; keep all other parameters identical.
measurements: Tensile testing for UTS and elongation
EBSD for grain morphology and misorientation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If preheated specimens do not show ≥10% reduction in warpage and porosity or do not exhibit statistically significant (p<0.05) increases in UTS or elongation versus ambient builds, the hypothesis is falsified.
